failure_summary.description: The agent added unsupported structure preservation to an abstract isomorphism conclusion and extrapolated a generic supercritical regime to a fixed-size conditioned law.
The agent selected a congruence modulo a proper divisor instead of respecting the full modulus and stated parameter range.

patch.reasoning: Add checks for two distinctions not stated explicitly in the current skill: abstract versus structure-preserving isomorphisms, and unconditioned versus fixed-size conditioned branching laws. The congruence failure is already directly covered by the existing full-modulus and range rule, so avoid duplicating it.

edits.content:
Separate the level of structure in a conclusion: an abstract graph isomorphism does not imply one that intertwines covering projections, deck actions, labels, roots, or decompositions. Require every added compatibility clause to be explicitly proved; symmetry in the hypotheses alone does not force an isomorphism to preserve the specified structure.

When a law is defined under fixed-size conditioning, do not infer its criticality from unconditioned weights or a generic phase diagram. Conditioning can induce a tilt, so distinguish the branching law of the conditioned object from an unconditioned process and state only the subcritical, critical, or supercritical regimes actually established, including their endpoint cases.
